about: Round 2 (Claude, 2026-11-05, on Kai's round-1 notes). Choruses + break: unchanged from r1 (2-beat cuts from the measured hits — 'timed brilliantly'). Everything else: every shot is [clip id, AT beat index, in-point s, why]; the beat index must be a strong beat (song-map.json 'strong'); a shot ends where the next begins. Each sung line starts a new shot on the strong beat nearest its first word (r1 started verse 1's shots 10 beats before the vocal, so every shot ran a line ahead). No photographic Karen anywhere (no face, no figure, no POV hands): abstract offices, phones, the paper trail, the TV world; Aarron and the band (mv-clip-1/16/17, st-new-25, mv-maybe-4 macro) are the recurring thread in the instrumental gaps.

intro: god's-eye Manhattan under the dial tone
'Thank you for calling' the towers light into a telephone
'your call is important to us' a phone blinks at an empty desk
'press three to speak to an adviser'
the band's instruments, close: sax keys, cymbal
'Three.' the band comes in: Aarron at the sampler
verse-1: the band: keyboard and upright bass
Aarron walks up with his DJ desk
'thirty years of service' her empty desk, her mug
'I can't authorise that' a clerk hangs up
'fetch me the desk that sits behind the desk'
the file goes up the hall
'nothing further I can do at this level'
'Sweetheart. There is always a level above the level.'
pre-chorus-1: 'So put down the script' a suited hand reaches
every clerk on the phone, into the hit
verse-2: 'Regional office, Thursday. Rain on the glass.'
'Borough office, Tuesday, they gave me a code'
'A caseworker will call you — nobody phoned.'
'he thinks I'll just throw in the towel' the phone goes down
Aarron at the sampler in the rain
'I know where it folds.' the sax
bridge: the city from above as the funk drops in
'Six weeks in a phone box on Lexington and Third'
'sun, snow, sun again, and not one word'
'The machine can do my job' the gold AI glitches
'here's the part they never printed in the manual'
'every system you ever built runs on people hanging up' people keep coming up the stairs
verse-3: 'this line is for emergencies' — 'look what I made'
the writers' room sees it on TV
'Chief of Staff at midnight, sounding tired and small'
'Karen. From the payphone.' the play count climbing
'That's all.' the writers' room, the show on the wall
outro: 'Hold, please.' over the courthouse into the night
up and away, to the last hit
